scope: Mobi iOS interop: maintained direct code plus unmerged pilot/candidate mechanisms

entries.title: Handwritten sealed-state visitors
entries.reason: The maintained direct integration cannot consume the qualified generated sealed-state API through its current build path.
entries.replacement: Use compiler-generated sealed cases in the actual feature presentation; delete the Kotlin visitor interfaces and Swift projections.
retirement_checks: Added, removed and changed payload cases fail when consumer handling is omitted.
Home, Nearby, Android and Shared UI preserve their behavior on the selected delivery.

entries.title: Unchecked Kotlin state sendability
entries.reason: The direct Nearby client declares the raw Kotlin state unchecked Sendable; that assertion does not provide compiler-checked isolation.
entries.replacement: Use compiler-checked actor ownership/native values or an upstream-supported safe state crossing; remove unchecked/preconcurrency declarations that are no longer needed.
retirement_checks: An off-actor raw state read and an unsafe Sendable container are rejected.
Actual feature transitions, equality and cross-runtime lifetime pass without unchecked Sendable.

entries.title: Numeric wire tags and decoders
entries.reason: The earlier pilot manually encodes variants and nullable payload combinations instead of consuming generated typed state.
entries.replacement: Delete the pilot wire protocol and decoders as real feature slices replace them; do not promote this protocol into production.
retirement_checks: No feature meaning depends on ordinal/tag tables.
The adopted app has one maintained path; historical evidence remains separately retained.

entries.title: Request-owner facades around suspend calls
entries.reason: The qualified supported path avoids broader generated async/error APIs while SwiftJob inheritance and KotlinError sendability findings remain unresolved.
entries.replacement: Use a qualified upstream async bridge, or a smaller operation-owned adapter; delete request registries and facade methods made redundant.
retirement_checks: Real service success, domain failure, cancellation and late completion preserve behavior.
No non-Sendable Kotlin result/error escapes isolation; unfinished work remains owned until completion.

entries.title: Opaque Nearby state handles
entries.reason: The current candidate keeps original Kotlin states in a dictionary and mirrors ownership with UUIDs, adoption and release calls.
entries.replacement: Assess an actor-owned original-state reference with native presentation; remove state IDs, the state dictionary and manual adopt/release bookkeeping if qualified.
retirement_checks: Actual TCA state/equality and the full map presentation compile without unsafe state crossing.
Replacement, cancellation and dropped results release references correctly; no lifetime/resource regression.

entries.title: Custom completion and drain transport
entries.reason: Native observation/disposal and detached cleanup compensate for the unqualified async bridge and the selected early-cancellation acknowledgement design.
entries.replacement: Prefer qualified structured async ownership; remove polling/listener registries and separate drain transport where redundant. Preserve actual-completion accounting for noncooperative work.
retirement_checks: Cancellation timing is explicit and tested.
Cancelling a waiter or ending a route cannot abandon unfinished backend work.
No polling loop/listener/drain registry remains solely for a retired bridge path.

entries.title: Closed generated API and experimental import checker
entries.reason: A private generated-module closure constrains unsupported API use; CheckImplementationOnly supplies an actively tested hidden-layout check on the assessed tuple.
entries.replacement: Use a supported narrow module/import recipe; remove experimental flag and unnecessary whole-feature module placement when equivalent enforcement is qualified.
retirement_checks: Raw API escape and invalid hidden-layout controls are rejected by the replacement recipe.
Actual consumer compile/link works without exposing Kotlin types or weakening diagnostics.

entries.title: Swift 5 coroutine-support compilation
entries.reason: The assessed generated coroutine support does not compile under the fully strict Swift 6 alternative; the selected profile keeps that module in Swift 5.
entries.replacement: Compile the affected support module in strict Swift 6 after upstream fixes; delete the per-module Swift 5 exception.
retirement_checks: Strict support compilation passes without suppressions, unsafe conformance patches or fallback.
The real app passes error/cancellation/isolation and delivery checks on that recipe.

entries.title: Runtime MainActor assertions and cancellation relay
entries.reason: The candidate adapts synchronous TCA dependency closures with assumeIsolated and relays cancellation back to a weak Store. This also reflects TCA and adapter design, not only Swift export.
entries.replacement: Use compiler-expressed actor contracts and ordinary feature-effect cancellation where supported; delete redundant assertions and relay tasks.
retirement_checks: The actual pinned TCA reducer/client compiles with checked isolation.
Cancellation reaches the intended feature without retaining its route or losing state restoration.

entries.title: Custom Swift-export producer and profile plumbing
entries.reason: The assessed standalone exporter/build path supplies module graphs, bridge compilation, modes and provenance outside a qualified supported Toolchain integration.
entries.replacement: Use supported build-tool integration; remove replaced exporter invocation, profile and module-order machinery while keeping repo-owned validation.
retirement_checks: Cold and relocated delivery builds preserve one Kotlin image, shared service identity, resources and native dependencies.
The default app and CI use the same maintained command; delegated Android bootstrap remains intact.

entries.title: Explicit macro-validation invocation override
entries.reason: The assessed owned build overrides an inherited macro-skip preference using an explicit Xcode argument. This is an environment control, not a Swift-export language limitation.
entries.replacement: Remove only the invocation override when the scoped build environment reliably validates macros; keep exact revision approvals and refusal controls.
retirement_checks: An unapproved locked macro is refused before the approved build succeeds.
No global preference change or skip-validation fallback is used.

entries.title: Private JVM temporary directories
entries.reason: Private temp ownership is a dependency-risk control for affected exporter/tool launches, not a repair of decoder/allocation vulnerabilities or a general Swift limitation.
entries.replacement: Reassess the exact affected graph after supported dependency remediation; remove vulnerability-specific plumbing only when its rationale and coverage are closed.
retirement_checks: Fresh selected-graph/advisory evidence supports the disposition.
Every affected JVM launch/descendant is accounted for; unrelated vulnerability findings are not marked fixed by temp handling.

entries.title: Serialized native feature tests
entries.reason: The pinned TCA 1.26.0 TestStore installs and restores a process-wide executor hook. Concurrent store lifetimes make these tests depend on shared scheduler state.
entries.replacement: Run the native feature suites concurrently when TCA provides per-test executor isolation; remove the serialized parent after qualifying the actual tests.
retirement_checks: Cold local and hosted runs plus repeated parallel Home/Nearby execution pass with the original time limits and exhaustive assertions.
Removing effect cancellation still fails the out-of-order completion test; cancellation or assertion failure leaves no pending test continuation.
